proposals.impact: lift open rate on lowest-performing automation toward Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: Money Worship automation sent 16 emails and achieved a 37.5% open rate. Money Vigilance sent only 12 but opened at 66.67%. Money Avoidance sits in the middle at 52.63%. The Worship sequence is the lowest performer and has the largest gap from the Vigilance benchmark. Subject line is the only variable Fred can shift in one file edit without touching send logic or audience segmentation.
proposals.proposal: The Money Worship subject line almost certainly leads with a concept ("Do you worship money?") rather than a specific, felt moment the reader recognises in themselves. Vigilance opens so strongly because vigilant types respond to precision and recognition. Worship types are more likely to open when the subject line names something they privately do — spending to feel secure, buying things before a difficult week — rather than asking them to self-identify with an abstract label. Rewrite email-01's subject line to a single concrete behaviour the worship pattern produces, in second person, no question mark required.

proposals.impact: restore daily content publishing pipeline blocked since 03:56 UTC
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 03:56 UTC on 22 August. With only one post queued and a 47-post published backlog, any further publishing failures leave the queue empty. The content pipeline is the primary organic discovery mechanism for the quiz. Zero quiz sessions in 48 hours is consistent with a broken top-of-funnel, and a failed blog workflow is a credible cause worth ruling out before attributing the zero to demand.
proposals.proposal: The workflow file itself is in the blocked paths list, so Fred cannot edit it directly. However, the failure is almost certainly caused by a runtime error in the script the workflow calls, not the workflow YAML itself. Check the workflow run logs at the GitHub Actions URL for run created 2026-08-22T03:56:07Z. The most common causes on a blog-post automation are an expired API key (OpenAI, Anthropia, or a CMS token), a changed environment variable name after a recent deploy, or a missing dependency after a package update. The single actionable file edit Fred can propose is refreshing or re-setting the relevant secret reference in the script the workflow calls.

proposals.impact: diagnose zero-session quiz window before funnel runs another 48h dark
proposals.observation: Zero quiz sessions and zero starts over a 48-hour window is a hard stop: nobody is reaching the quiz page, or the page is rendering broken for all visitors. The recent blog posts from June suggest scheduled publishing is weeks ahead of today (22 August) which means no new organic entries have appeared in over two months. The quiz index page almost certainly has a call-to-action or a meta tag that is either not indexed or is pointing traffic to a path that no longer resolves. One file edit to verify the canonical URL and the primary CTA href on the quiz landing page is worth doing before Joel spends time on any paid traffic.
proposals.proposal: Audit the quiz index page for two things in one pass: first, confirm the canonical href in the head matches the actual deployed URL exactly (no trailing slash mismatch, no staging subdomain left in); second, confirm the primary CTA button href points to quiz step one and not a redirect that dropped during a recent deploy. If the canonical is wrong, search engines are splitting authority across two URLs. If the CTA href is broken, every visitor who lands correctly still cannot start. Either fix resolves in a single line change.
